component.name: Apache Creadur RAT
component.description: Build-time / CLI license-auditing tool: RAT (Release Audit Tool) walks a source tree, matches files against configurable license/header definitions, and reports unapproved or unknown licenses. It runs as a CLI, an Ant task, or a Maven plugin, always in the developer's or CI's own process, never as a network service. The threat model is written in creadur-rat and covers the Creadur dev-tool family; the sibling tools Whisker (license-documentation generator) and Tentacles (release-bundle analyzer) share RAT's trust profile.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: RAT audit run
blueprints.description: Data flow described by the threat model: a trusted caller invokes RAT (CLI/Ant/Maven) on a directory and a configuration; RAT reads the configuration, walks the tree, descends into archives, matches licenses, and writes a report. The boundary is the input RAT is pointed at; RAT's security questions only arise when that input is untrusted (for example CI auditing an untrusted contribution or a downloaded third-party artifact).

assets.name: RAT process
assets.description: The RAT run inside the developer's or CI's own process: the Reporter and walkers, the XMLConfigurationReader, and the ArchiveWalker (Apache Commons Compress ArchiveStreamFactory) that reads archive entries into an in-memory buffer, never extracting them to disk.

assets.name: Scanned tree, archives, and configuration
assets.description: The tree being audited (file content and paths, including zip/jar/tar archives RAT descends into) and the RAT configuration (XML/text license and matcher definitions). The configuration is operator-trusted; the scanned files may be untrusted.

zones.name: Scanned input
zones.description: Files, archives, and (if attacker-supplied) configuration processed by a RAT run; untrusted when RAT audits third-party contributions or artifacts.

zones.name: Trusted invocation
zones.description: The developer or CI job invoking RAT, the invocation arguments, and the build environment; trusted by assumption.

assumptions.description: A JRE; RAT reads the filesystem it is pointed at and writes a report. It opens no network connections and runs no services; the one operator-reachable exception is an XSLT stylesheet using xsl:include to pull a remote resource, and XSLT stylesheets are trusted, operator-controlled configuration.

RAT configuration (XSLT stylesheets, config files, license definitions, custom matchers) is trusted and operator-controlled; the scanned files may be untrusted (maintainer-confirmed in the PR #677 review).
XML parser behaviour depends on the platform JAXP and is configurable via the standard JAXP system properties; RAT disables external entities by default.
The CLI, Ant task, and Maven plugin front-ends are generated from a common option core, so any security-relevant behaviour or gap in that core transfers automatically to all three UIs.

threats.name: Decompression bomb / archive resource exhaustion
threats.description: The archive walker extracts entry contents into an in-memory buffer (Apache Commons Compress ArchiveStreamFactory) held until the document is processed, with no decompression, size, depth, or entry-count bound, so a crafted archive can exhaust memory (OOM). Maintainer-confirmed as not bounded; the model records this as a disclaimed gap plus a downstream responsibility: runs over untrusted archives must be sandboxed or resource-limited. Path traversal on archive entry names does not apply because entries are never extracted to disk.

threats.name: XXE via attacker-supplied XML configuration
threats.description: A crafted RAT XML configuration triggers external-entity resolution (file read / SSRF), critical when the configuration is untrusted. Mitigated: the config reader has external entities disabled (RAT-560), with DOCTYPE handling further hardened by PR #679. A break of this provided property via untrusted input on a realistic run is a VALID finding.

threats.name: Unexpected outbound connection from a RAT run
threats.description: RAT claims no ambient network or side effects: it does filesystem I/O only and opens no network connections on default settings (sole exception: an operator-supplied XSLT xsl:include pointing at a remote resource, which is trusted configuration). An unexpected outbound connection would violate this provided property.

threats.name: Findings requiring input the operator already trusts
threats.description: Attacks that require the operator to feed RAT input they already control are out of model (OUT-OF-MODEL: trusted-input). This covers the dominant intended case of auditing one's own source tree, RAT's operator-invoked header-insertion write mode (--addLicense, whose header text comes from the operator-controlled license definition, not the scanned tree), operator-defined custom matchers reading scanned text, and operator-set XSLT stylesheets. An attacker who controls the RAT invocation or the trusted source tree already owns the build.

threats.name: Treating a clean RAT report as a security sign-off
threats.description: RAT checks license compliance; it is not a vulnerability scanner or a security gate, and a clean RAT report says nothing about security. 'RAT didn't catch X security issue' is out of purpose, and a missed or false license match is a correctness bug, not a vulnerability (unless it crosses a resource bound).

trustBoundaries.name: Untrusted-input trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: The boundary is the input RAT is pointed at (files and configuration). A finding is in-model only if it is triggered by untrusted input (a hostile file, archive, or config) that a realistic RAT deployment processes, for example CI auditing an untrusted PR.

controls.name: XML configuration parsing with external entities disabled
controls.description: The XML configuration reader disables external entities by default (RAT-560); DOCTYPE handling is further hardened by PR #679. This is a hardcoded behaviour, not an operator knob.

controls.name: No ambient network or side effects
controls.description: RAT runs locally and only opens files; it opens no network connections and runs no services. Build tooling (Maven/Ant) may fetch dependencies, but RAT itself does not.

controls.name: Sandbox and resource-limit untrusted-input runs
controls.description: When auditing untrusted input (CI on untrusted PRs, third-party artifacts), run RAT with resource limits or in a sandbox, and do not feed it attacker-controlled configuration. For the operator's own trusted source tree (the normal case) no special handling is needed.

controls.name: Keep RAT updated and pinned
controls.description: Keep RAT updated and pin the version in the build.
